title: How to add Custom User Properties in ASP.NET Core Identity
description: Extend the Identity user model with custom properties like Age, Country, and Salary.

data.text: The default IdentityUser class stores common fields like UserName, Email, and PasswordHash, but real-world apps often need more — Age, Department, Country, or any business-specific data. Adding custom properties to AppUser is straightforward: declare them as new properties and run a new EF Core migration.

terms.definition: Your custom Identity user class. Adding new auto-properties here automatically maps them as new columns in AspNetUsers.
A snapshot of model changes. Running AddMigration then UpdateDatabase adds the new columns to the database.
The underlying SQL table that stores all Identity user records, including any custom columns you add.

data.text: Extend AppUser.cs with the extra fields. EF Core will detect them as new columns the next time a migration is generated. Here we add Age (int), Country (an enum), and Salary (string with [Required]).

data.title: AppUser.cs — extended with custom properties
Nullable reference types
data.text: If your project uses nullable reference types, append ? to string properties like Salary if they are optional. The [Required] attribute takes precedence for validation.
After adding the properties, create a new migration so EF Core generates the ALTER TABLE statements that add the new columns to AspNetUsers.

data.title: Add and apply migration
data.code:
dotnet ef migrations add AddCustomUserFields
dotnet ef database update

data.caption: How a custom property travels from form to database
data.definition:
flowchart LR
    F[Create/Update Form] -->|POST| C[AdminController]
    C -->|maps to| U[AppUser instance]
    U -->|CreateAsync / UpdateAsync| M[UserManager<AppUser>]
    M -->|INSERT / UPDATE| DB[(AspNetUsers table)]
    DB -->|new columns: Age, Country, Salary| S[Stored in DB]

data.title: Exercise: Add a Department Property
data.description: Extend your Identity setup by adding a Department string property to AppUser.
steps: Add public string Department { get; set; } to AppUser.cs.
Run dotnet ef migrations add AddDepartment and dotnet ef database update.
Update the Create and Update views to include a Department input.
Update the Create and Update actions to accept and save Department.
Create a new user and confirm the Department column is populated in AspNetUsers.
data.expectedOutcome: The AspNetUsers table has a new Department column, and users can be created and edited with a department value.

items.text: New property declared on AppUser class
AspNetUsers table has the new column
items.hint: Verify in SQL Server Object Explorer.

items.text: Create action maps new fields to AppUser
Update action also handles the new fields

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Add any auto-property to AppUser to add a new column to AspNetUsers.
A new EF Core migration is required for every schema change.
Update Create and Update actions to accept and map the new values.
IdentityResult should always be checked after user manager operations.
data.takeaway: You can now extend the Identity user with any domain-specific fields. Next, learn to control who can access what with roles.
